I am 67 years old, and I have farmed these fields for more than 40 years. I only finished primary school, but I know the soil and weather of Quzhou County better than any book. My children have gone to work in the city, so it is just me and my wife managing the land now. I have 8 mu of flat, good-quality land. At my age, I do not want to take risks with new crops or heavy labour like cotton or vegetables, which need constant pruning and many pesticide sprays. I will stick to the wheat–maize rotation that everyone here relies on, because the buyers come to the village every year, the prices are stable, and the work fits what my wife and I can still handle.

The winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. I sowed an improved variety, *shimai22*, at about 30 jin per mu, and I did rotary tillage before sowing. This spring I will top-dress it with urea and irrigate three or four times total (including the winter irrigation I already gave it and the green-up, jointing, and filling irrigations). I will spray for weeds once, insects twice, and maybe a fungicide if the weather turns humid. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize, *denghai605*, using no-tillage direct seeding—this saves me labour and fuel, and the village technician says the yields are just as good. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate twice during the summer, spraying for insects and weeds as needed. I expect around 1,120 jin per mu from the maize.
